PC: Identify the patient’s chief concern and patient needs
Explore precipitating factors contributing to the patient’s presentation
Assess for current suicidal ideation and baseline suicidal thoughts (if applicable)

Complete a safety plan with the patient, including: limiting access to lethal means (which could include locking up medications and sharps), increasing family supervision, and utilizing supports, including crisis resources, when needed.
MK: Borderline personality disorder - leading diagnosis. Patient with history of chronic passive suicidal ideation, self-harm, impulsive behavior, low self-esteem, and concerns with abandonment

Substance (alcohol)-induced mood disorder: patient with depressed mood and suicidal thoughts in the setting of consistent alcohol use (though more today). However, few clear depressive symptoms noted/reported. * Unspecified mood disorder - rule out major depressive disorder, adjustment disorder with depressed mood, and bipolar disorder: patient with mood symptoms requiring further diagnostic clarification (ie, number of depressive symptoms/their time course and further characterization of mood lability to rule out hypomanic/manic episodes)
SBP: Disposition: home considering higher level of care such as partial hospitalization program (PHP) or intensive outpatient program (IOP)
ICS: Greet patient, state name, and state role being clear and concise
Respect the patient’s personal space and be approachable
Offer validation and reinforce that the patient is safe
Appropriate support should be provided to the patient throughout the interview.
